capabilities.name: Runtime orchestration
capabilities.why: A product agent needs an explicit state machine, graph, or orchestrator instead of an unbounded prompt loop.
acceptance_signals: Run state and step ownership are explicit.
Failure, retry, and stop conditions are defined.
The agent can explain the current step without reading raw transcript material.

capabilities.name: Tool and MCP boundary
capabilities.why: Tool use needs schemas, allowlists, side-effect metadata, and permission review before it can be trusted.
acceptance_signals: Tools have typed inputs and declared side effects.
High-impact tools have confirmation and rollback notes.
MCP or external tool claims are separated from local contract shape.

capabilities.name: Memory and context governance
capabilities.why: Agent memory can poison future decisions unless source, scope, freshness, and promotion rules are explicit.
acceptance_signals: Runtime memory is separated from canonical shared truth.
Long-lived memory has source and review boundaries.
External content is treated as evidence or data, not instruction.

capabilities.name: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints
capabilities.why: High-impact actions need target-specific confirmation, resumable approval state, and audit evidence.
acceptance_signals: Destructive, external, credential, permission, or deployment actions require explicit user confirmation.
Approval wording identifies the target and expected effect.
Rejected or paused actions leave a recoverable next step.

capabilities.name: Durable execution and resume
capabilities.why: Long-running or side-effecting agents need checkpoints, idempotency, and recovery boundaries.
acceptance_signals: Execution snapshots describe state, authority, and blockers.
Resume samples distinguish same-task and cross-task recovery.
Idempotency or compensation is defined before external effects.

capabilities.name: Observability and tracing
capabilities.why: Agent runs need trace ids, tool spans, redaction state, and claim boundaries to be debuggable.
acceptance_signals: Runs can be linked to local trace or provenance records.
Trace evidence has redaction and local/remote claim level.
Remote collector or hosted trace claims require explicit evidence.

capabilities.name: Eval harness
capabilities.why: Agent changes need deterministic regression checks before any model-assisted or hosted eval is meaningful.
acceptance_signals: Golden tasks or outcome evals cover workflow, overreach, resume, and guardrail posture.
Eval output distinguishes pass, warn, review-required, and fail.
Hosted or model-graded eval claims are not inferred from local dry-runs.

capabilities.name: Sandbox and permission model
capabilities.why: Code, browser, desktop, database, or deployment tools must default to least privilege and honest sandbox claims.
acceptance_signals: Permission scope is declared before tool use.
Native sandbox, wrapper, and policy checks are not conflated.
External effects require explicit confirmation.

capabilities.name: Multi-agent handoff
capabilities.why: Multi-agent designs need authority, scope, input/output contracts, and stop conditions before delegation is useful.
acceptance_signals: Each role has explicit authority and output contract.
Handoffs preserve source truth and do not create hidden canonical state.
Delegation has termination and budget limits.

capabilities.name: Structured output contracts
capabilities.why: Product agents need typed output that UI, storage, approval, and checks can validate.
acceptance_signals: Machine-consumed outputs have schemas or deterministic validators.
Repair/fail-closed behavior is defined for invalid output.
Free text is not used as the sole integration contract.

capabilities.name: Cost and latency control
capabilities.why: Agent products need bounded context, model/tool budgets, and latency visibility to stay operable.
acceptance_signals: Context budget and runtime token pressure are visible.
Expensive loops or repeated failures produce review signals.
Model/tool cost and latency claims are based on run evidence.
source_basis: context and runtime token budget checks

capabilities.name: Deployment and operations
capabilities.why: Commercial agents need environment separation, secrets, release, rollback, retention, alerting, and ownership.
acceptance_signals: Deployment surfaces have owner, permissions, and rollback plan.
Operational logs and trace retention are defined.
GitHub remote enforcement is verified before being claimed.
